subject: Acme Analytics — throughput & latency follow-up / POC next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Taylor <sarah.taylor@acme.io>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Acme call recap — throughput / latency notes + next steps

Thanks again for the time today, Sarah — good conversation. Quick recap of what I captured and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Summary of requirements (from call)
- Peak concurrent QPS: ~120 QPS during peak daily windows
- Typical sustained QPS: ~30-50 QPS
- Latency target: p95 generation time < 120 ms for single-turn requests (most requests are 64-128 token responses)
- Data sensitivity: PII in prompts; SOC 2 required; not yet blocked on VPC but procurement will evaluate security posture

Options we discussed
- Hosted API: fastest onboarding, pay-as-you-go, built-in model catalog. Good if you want to iterate quickly, but can have variability in throughput during noisy neighbor events unless we set routing to dedicated pools.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale; supports autoscaling and burst capacity; simplest path to meet p95 SLAs for consistent high QPS.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): for locked-down regulatory needs — more setup time and contract work.

My read: given a 120 QPS peak and strict p95 target, Dedicated reserved capacity looks like the safest POC to prove performance while you ramp. Hosted can be used for early experimentation, but we'd expect a more controlled Dedicated proof for production acceptance.

Next steps
1) Can you confirm the 120 QPS peak and share an anonymized sample traffic profile (minute-by-minute QPS or a 24h histogram)? If you can attach that, we can size the pool more accurately.
2) Lauren — can you draft an initial Dedicated sizing estimate and delta vs Hosted for a 6-week POC?
3) Aisha — can you coordinate procurement touchpoint and share any template contract timing we should expect?
4) Sarah — I attached a lightweight POC options spreadsheet for comparison. If config/contract resources look good, propose a short kickoff next Tue 2026-07-14 at 10:00 PT.

Attachments: poc-options-compare.xlsx (spreadsheet comparing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private); acme-requirements-summary.pdf

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

From: Sarah Taylor <sarah.taylor@acme.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.io>
Date: Wed, 8 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme call recap — throughput / latency notes + next steps

Thanks Ben — recap looks accurate. A few clarifications from our side:

- Peak: 120 QPS is correct; that occurs for roughly 30-45 minutes after our product releases. Typical daily sustained is ~40 QPS.
- Latency: p95 target of 120 ms is a hard requirement for the feature owner; p99 ideally < 250 ms.
- Traffic shape: bursts are short but frequent; we can share a 48h anonymized logs export (no PII) by end of day tomorrow.
- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II is required; we are evaluating private network options but would prefer Hosted or Dedicated if logs/audit meet our needs.
- Procurement: procurement@acme.io is my contact; they will send a standard vendor questionnaire once we have an initial SOW.

We are open to a Dedicated trial if you can provide a trial sizing and preliminary SLA language for p95. If Hosted + routing policy can guarantee the p95 for the 120 QPS window, that would be attractive given time-to-market.

I can do Tue 14 Jul 10:00 PT for kickoff.

Best,
Sarah
Product Lead, ML Experiences
Acme Analytics

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Acme sizing / commercial ask (please advise)

Lauren / Aisha — short internal note based on Sarah's reply.

Key asks from Acme: 120 QPS peak; p95 < 120 ms; SOC2 required; procurement will want an SOW and questionnaire. They prefer Hosted if it can meet the p95 but are comfortable doing a Dedicated trial.

Recommendation (initial):
- Propose a 6-week Dedicated reserved pool sized for sustained 60 QPS with bursting to 140 QPS for short windows. That gives headroom for the 120 QPS peaks while keeping cost reasonable.
- Provide an alternate Hosted config: route their traffic through a semi-dedicated pool with prefix caching and KV warmers; include a performance SLA pilot for the POC duration. If we can demonstrate p95 < 120ms in Hosted during POC, conversion to Hosted for prod is an option.

Lauren — please provide:
- Ballpark GPU pool sizing (gpus, instance types) and expected token/sec per GPU for the proposed config.
- Estimated monthly cost for Dedicated POC vs projected Hosted spend for the same workload.

Aisha — please:
- Draft a short SOW template for a 6-week POC and note any standard contract caveats for trial Dedicated pools.
- Flag procurement contacts and expected cycles so we can push the kickoff date if needed.

I'll loop Sarah once we have the sizing + SOW draft.

Thanks,
Ben

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Taylor <sarah.taylor@acme.io>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.io>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme call recap — throughput / latency notes + next steps

Sarah — thanks for confirming. Based on your numbers, we've prepared a short proposal for a pragmatic POC that balances speed and predictability:

Proposed POC: 6-week Dedicated reserved pool (recommended)
- Size: pool sized for sustained 60 QPS with autoscale bursts to 150 QPS for short windows (covers 120 QPS peaks)
- SLA: p95 target < 120 ms for configured request profile; we'll instrument with tracing and token-level cost breakdowns
- Security: SOC 2 evidence and audit logs will be provided; optional private networking for the next phase
- Success criteria: sustained p95 < 120 ms across peak windows and stable error rate < 0.5% over 7 consecutive days

Alternative (if you prefer Hosted pilot):
- Semi-dedicated routing for Hosted with prefix caching and priority routing during peak windows; we will run a 2-week ramp to validate p95 and then decide on Dedicated if needed.

Attachments: poc-options-compare.xlsx; acme-requirements-summary.pdf
DocuSign envelope: https://www.docusign.com/en/transactions/ABC123456789 (SOW + trial terms draft attached)

Can you confirm:
1) Agreement to proceed with the 6-week Dedicated trial OR preference for Hosted pilot?
2) Procurement contact and any vendor questionnaire timelines?
3) Availability for kickoff Tues 14 Jul at 10:00 PT?

If agreed, Lauren will share the sizing/cost estimate and Aisha will share the SOW/DocuSign draft by Mon EOD 2026-07-13.

Looking forward — Ben
